summary: Douglas County lookout: a 20-foot pole L-4 tower dated 1939 and removed in 1966; a 2016 hiking blog reports four concrete footings left on the summit.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Umpqua National Forest
facts.status_note: Tower removed in 1966; a 2016 hiking blog reports only four concrete footings left on the summit.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Oregon Lookouts page dates the tower to an undetermined time after 1936 and mentions 1920s use without details; the register, firelookout.com and the 2016 blog give 1939. The 1939 date fits the after-1936 estimate.
The register and the 2016 blog say removed in 1966; firelookout.com says destroyed. All three give 1966.

notes_for_editor: The remains statement (four concrete footings) rests on a single 2016 hiking blog; no current source was found, so verify before publishing. The record's height_m 6.1 (20 ft) matches the register and firelookout.com; no change. 'Pole' (register, blog) and 'round timber' (Oregon Lookouts) are treated as compatible, not as a conflict. The Oregon Lookouts 1920s line has no detail and is kept only as a decade note. The Forest Service trail page we read shows no closure. The register's 1939-1966 photo caption (Verschoor collection) is not added as a photo. The Forest Service says excellent views include Cinnamon Butte Lookout; the 2016 blog says the view needs a walk off the summit through trees, so the story reports the view with that caveat.
